note: Each composer's shared period: the level a narrow unit falls back to after the composer (TRAINING.md, section 4), and where the caps are counted (a composer's tenth, a collection's third). The sheet's period (the Composer Pool Sieve's Period column) where the sheet has the composer; otherwise by the year of birth, with the sheet's boundaries read from its own composers: before 1570, Before 1600; to 1709, Baroque; to 1779, Classical; to 1859, Romantic; to 1899, 1890 to 1950 (Monteverdi, born 1567, is before 1600; Pergolesi, 1710, Baroque; C. P. E. Bach, 1714, Classical; Field, 1782, Romantic; Debussy, 1862, 1890 to 1950). A composer known only by the year of a dated work is taken as born thirty years before it. Years of birth are the collections' own where they give one (OpenScore's composer list, Mutopia's composer pages and headers, the Josquin Research Project's records), else the standard ones. Written on 21 November 2026 for score-reader's catalogue version 16 (version 17 adds 18 of the sheet's composers, each in the sheet's period); a judgment table: a composer the rule places wrongly is corrected here, with the reason. Catalogue version 22 adds 341: the seven of DCML's version 19 corpora (Frescobaldi, Schütz, Medtner, Koželuch, Sweelinck, W. F. Bach, Peri) by the year of birth, and the Polish Scores' composers by the dates the collection gives: a birth year, or one about it; for a composer it knows only as active (born before a year, died after one), born about 30 years before the first (as Mr. Powlwheel); for one it knows only by the year of death, born about 50 years before it. 53 composers of the Polish Scores whom it gives no years are in neither table: they count at the level of everything only, until their years are found.
